title: Gate result
description: Outcome of a release Gate evaluation. The result value controls whether a deploy may proceed; new result values require a major version bump. The vocabulary is shared by `result` and `checks[].status` and each value carries the same meaning at both levels.

result.description: Aggregate gate outcome, drawn from the same vocabulary as checks[].status. passed: the gate ran and every asserted check passed. failed: an attempted check reported a failure. errored: a check could not be evaluated to a verdict. skipped: a check was proven not to apply; this is an exemption, not an absence of evidence. review_required: a human decision is still open and no one has decided the outcome. unbound: the check was asserted and no command was ever bound to it, so nothing ran; this is a configuration defect and is never an exemption. A consumer MUST NOT read `skipped` and `unbound` alike, and MUST NOT read `review_required` as a decision already taken.

subject_ref.description: Identifier of the run, build, or change set being gated.

status.description: One check's outcome, drawn from the same vocabulary as result: passed, failed, errored, skipped, review_required, or unbound. The same six values with the same claims, and no additional meaning at check level. An unbound check is reported here rather than omitted, so a consumer counting checks sees every check the gate asserted.
